sentences.en: From NPR, this is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是NPR，我是“隐藏的大脑”。

sentences.en: The week has just begun in Keystone, Iowa.
sentences.zh: 新的一周刚刚在爱荷华州基斯通拉开帷幕。

sentences.en: We're here to bear witness to a family meeting.
sentences.zh: 我们来到这里，是为了见证一场家庭会议。
如果你愿意的话，也可以说是一场干预。

sentences.en: It got kind of rough towards the end of the week, didn't it?
sentences.zh: 到这周快结束时，情况变得有点棘手了，不是吗？

sentences.en: We didn't feel like such a family, did we?
sentences.zh: 我们感觉不像是一个家庭了，对吧？

sentences.en: Rachel Cruzee is running this meeting.
sentences.zh: 蕾切尔·克鲁齐正在主持这场会议。

sentences.en: The other participants are gathered around her in a circle.
sentences.zh: 其他参与者围成一圈坐在她周围。

sentences.en: A couple of them fidget, but most listen attentively.
sentences.zh: 他们中有几个人有些局促不安，但大多数都在专心聆听。

sentences.en: So on Friday, we decided that today we needed to have a family meeting.
sentences.zh: 所以就在周五，我们决定今天需要开个家庭会议。

sentences.en: All right, so this weekend, I found this book, and it's called It's Mine.
sentences.zh: 好的，这个周末我找到了这本书，书名叫《是我的》。

sentences.en: So when I read this book, I want you to think about how last week went and how this week could go.
sentences.zh: 所以当我读这本书时，我希望大家想一想上周过得怎么样，以及这周可以怎么过。

sentences.en: This family meeting is taking place in a kindergarten classroom in a rural part of eastern Iowa.
sentences.zh: 这场家庭会议正在爱荷华州东部农村地区的一间幼儿园教室里进行。

sentences.en: Rachel is the teacher, and the lesson she wants to share is one that could have a lasting impact on her students.
sentences.zh: 蕾切尔是老师，她想分享的这堂课可能会对她的学生产生深远的影响。

sentences.en: The story is set on an island.
sentences.zh: 故事发生在一个小岛上。

sentences.en: On the island live three quarrelsome frogs named Milton, Rupert, and Lydia.
sentences.zh: 岛上住着三只爱吵架的青蛙，名叫弥尔顿、鲁珀特和莉迪亚。

sentences.en: They quarreled and quibbled from dawn to dusk.
sentences.zh: 他们从日出到日落争吵不休。

sentences.en: They said, stay out of the pond, yelled Milton.
sentences.zh: 弥尔顿大喊：“离池塘远点！”

sentences.en: The island, shouted Rupert, the earth is mine.
sentences.zh: 鲁珀特大喊：“岛屿，土地是我的。”

sentences.en: Then a flood swallows up the island.
sentences.zh: 接着，一场洪水吞没了小岛。

sentences.en: There was only one rock left, and there the frogs huddled, trembling from cold and fright.
sentences.zh: 只剩下一块岩石，青蛙们缩在上面，冷得和吓得瑟瑟发抖。

sentences.en: But they felt better now that they were together, sharing the same fears and hopes.
sentences.zh: 但现在他们在一起了，分担着同样的恐惧和希望，这让他们感觉好多了。

sentences.en: The frogs swim together, hop off to butterflies, and rest in the weeds.
sentences.zh: 青蛙们一起游泳，跳着去追蝴蝶，在杂草中休息。

sentences.en: Right, we can work together, can't we?
sentences.zh: 对吧，我们可以一起合作，对吗？

sentences.en: Because at the beginning of the story, when they were saying, it's mine, it's mine, was anybody having fun?
sentences.zh: 因为在故事刚开始的时候，当他们说“这是我的，这是我的”时，有人觉得开心吗？

sentences.en: The frogs are happier when they stop being selfish.
sentences.zh: 当青蛙不再自私时，它们会更快乐。

sentences.en: This is what it looks like to teach what are sometimes called soft skills.
sentences.zh: 这就是教授有时被称为软技能的课程的样子。

sentences.en: The kind of skills that kids don't get asked about on tests.
sentences.zh: 孩子们在考试中不会被问到的那种技能。

sentences.en: Of course, Rachel teaches the other things you'd expect.
sentences.zh: 当然，蕾切尔也会教其他你意料之中的内容。

sentences.en: But lessons like this one about the selfish frogs might have the greatest impact.
sentences.zh: 但像这样关于自私青蛙的课程可能会产生最大的影响。

sentences.en: In fact, this impact can actually be quantified in dollars.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这种影响实际上可以用金钱来衡量。

sentences.en: Today we ask some questions with big implications.
sentences.zh: 今天我们提出一些意义重大的问题。

sentences.en: Can you put an economic value on a great kindergarten teacher?
sentences.zh: 你能为一个伟大的幼儿园老师赋予经济价值吗？

sentences.en: How is it that two children living just a few blocks from each other can have radically different chances in life?
sentences.zh: 为什么两个仅仅相隔几个街区的孩子，在生活中的机遇会有天壤之别？

sentences.en: What is it that gives Salt Lake City an edge over Cleveland when it comes to offering people a better life than their parents?
sentences.zh: 是什么让盐湖城在为人们提供比父母更好的生活方面，比克利夫兰更有优势？

sentences.en: The state of your American dream, this week on Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 你的美国梦现状，本周“隐藏的大脑”。

sentences.en: The stories we tell about ourselves, stories of success and stories of failure, often have their beginnings in the distant paSt.
sentences.zh: 我们讲述的关于自己的故事，成功的故事和失败的故事，往往都起源于遥远的过去。
有时是在我们的童年时期。

sentences.en: Sometimes before we were even born.
sentences.zh: 有时甚至在我们出生之前。

sentences.en: My guest today has explored this idea using hard data drawn from tens of millions of people.
sentences.zh: 我今天的嘉宾利用从数千万人口中提取的硬数据探讨了这个观点。

sentences.en: It's difficult to describe the range of things he does, except to say that Raj Chetty, an economist at Harvard University,
sentences.zh: 很难描述他所做事情的范围，只能说拉吉·切蒂，这位哈佛大学的经济学家，

sentences.en: might be the foremost authority today on the state of the American dream.
sentences.zh: 可能是当今美国梦现状领域最权威的专家。
拉吉，欢迎来到“隐藏的大脑”。

sentences.en: It's a pleasure to be here.
I want to begin by looking at snapshots in time, Raj.
sentences.zh: 拉吉，我想从审视时间切片开始。

sentences.en: And these are moments from your own life that I think explain a great deal about your work.
sentences.zh: 这些是你自己生活中的时刻，我认为它们很大程度上解释了你的工作。

sentences.en: The first snapshot is when you're living in New Delhi in India and you go to see the Taj Mahal.
sentences.zh: 第一个切片是你住在印度新德里的时候，你去看泰姬陵。

sentences.en: It's a few hours from your home in Delhi.
sentences.zh: 离你在德里的家有几个小时的路程。

sentences.en: Well, it was the first time I'd been to the Taj Mahal.
sentences.zh: 嗯，那是我第一次去泰姬陵。

sentences.en: And, you know, of course, like everyone, it's overwhelming in its beauty and how impressive of a monument it is.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，当然和所有人一样，它的美以及它作为一座纪念碑的宏伟震撼人心。

sentences.en: But I think what I was most struck by is after then coming back out of the monument, which was very immaculately kept and maintained,
sentences.zh: 但我想我感触最深的是，在参观完这座一尘不染、维护极佳的纪念碑出来之后，

sentences.en: seeing the abject poverty outside the Taj Mahal, people begging for money, kids who don't have clothes, who are on the street, you know, don't have adequate food.
sentences.zh: 看到了泰姬陵外面赤裸裸的贫困，人们乞讨金钱，没有衣服穿、流落街头的孩子，你知道的，没有充足的食物。

sentences.en: Certainly, I was exposed to inequality, you know, throughout childhood.
sentences.zh: 当然，我在整个童年时期都接触过不平等。

sentences.en: But I think this was just such a vivid version of it that stuck in my mind for many years.
sentences.zh: 但我想这是极其生动的一种体验，多年来一直留在我脑海中。

sentences.en: A couple of years after you visit the Taj Mahal, your family immigrates to the United States.
sentences.zh: 在你参观泰姬陵几年后，你的家庭移民到了美国。

sentences.en: You're in a private school in Milwaukee.
sentences.zh: 你在密尔沃基的一所私立学校。

sentences.en: You play tennis and chess, and so you visit other schools in the area for competitions.
sentences.zh: 你打网球和国际象棋，所以你会去该地区的其他学校参加比赛。
所以，其实是一次相似的经历。

sentences.en: So, I went to a private school on the north side of Milwaukee called University School.
sentences.zh: 我去了密尔沃基北区的一所私立学校，叫做大学学校。

sentences.en: And we'd compete with other schools, and as you said, in tennis and chess.
sentences.zh: 我们会和其他学校比赛，正如你所说，比网球和国际象棋。

sentences.en: And you just see, again, the remarkable differences in the physical structure of these schools.
sentences.zh: 你再次看到了这些学校在物理结构上的显著差异。

sentences.en: So, the school that I went to was on something like 150-acre campus with lots of college-level classes.
sentences.zh: 我去的学校占地大约150英亩，有很多大学水平的课程。

sentences.en: And in contrast, you know, the schools we'd visit were public schools in the city of Milwaukee, which, as you might know, these are schools that have faced a lot of challenges.
sentences.zh: 相比之下，你知道的，我们参观的学校是密尔沃基市的公立学校，正如你可能知道的，这些学校面临着很多挑战。

sentences.en: And that was just evident, you know, as a child, seeing the opportunities kids there had, talking to them about the types of classes they could take.
sentences.zh: 作为一个孩子，这是显而易见的，看到那里的孩子拥有的机会，和他们聊聊他们能上的课程类型。

sentences.en: Like, again, just really seeing a world with tremendous inequity and wondering, you know, how did I end up in this position?
sentences.zh: 就像，再次真正看到了一个存在巨大不平等的世界，并纳闷，你知道的，我怎么会落到这个位置？

sentences.en: And how did these kids, who at some level were very similar, were sitting on different sides of the chessboard,
sentences.zh: 而这些孩子，在某种程度上非常相似，却坐在棋盘的不同两端，

sentences.en: how did they end up in a different position in terms of what they had in opportunities?
sentences.zh: 他们在拥有的机会方面，怎么会落入不同的境地？

sentences.en: So, let's take these ideas from these snapshots, you know, questions related to inequality, to segregation, to opportunity,
sentences.zh: 所以，让我们从这些切片中汲取这些想法，你知道的，与不平等、隔离、机遇相关的问题，

sentences.en: and dive into some of the research that you've conducted.
sentences.zh: 并深入探讨你进行的一些研究。

sentences.en: You once did a study that determined the precise value of having a great kindergarten teacher.
sentences.zh: 你曾经做过一项研究，测算出了拥有一个伟大的幼儿园老师的确切价值。

sentences.en: Tell me about that study and what the value is that you computed.
sentences.zh: 跟我讲讲那项研究，以及你计算出的价值是什么。

sentences.en: Yeah, so social scientists have for a long time been studying and been interested in understanding how education affects kids' outcomes.
sentences.zh: 是的，社会学家长期以来一直在研究并有兴趣了解教育如何影响孩子的结果。

sentences.en: Most prior studies that have been done look at impacts on outcomes like test scores.
sentences.zh: 之前做过的大多数研究都着眼于对考试成绩等结果的影响。

sentences.en: So, if you have a better teacher, for instance, or if you're in a smaller classroom, do you do better as measured by standardized tests?
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你有一个更好的老师，或者如果你在一个更小的教室里，通过标准化考试来衡量，你会表现得更好吗？

sentences.en: Now, one of the puzzling findings from that earlier work is that you tend to find that if you're in what you might think of as a better classroom, let's take as a concrete example,
sentences.zh: 现在，早期研究中令人困惑的一个发现是，你往往会发现，如果你身处你可能认为是更好的教室里，我们以一个具体例子来说明，

sentences.en: classroom with a smaller number of kids.
sentences.zh: 一个孩子数量较少的教室。

sentences.en: You tend to see that kids in those types of classes tend to have higher test scores at the end of that school year, but those gains quickly fade away.
sentences.zh: 你往往会看到，在这些类型的班级里的孩子在该学年结束时往往有更高的考试成绩，但这些收益很快就会消退。

sentences.en: So, that is, if I was in a better kindergarten classroom, I'm doing better at the end of kindergarten, but only a little better at the end of first grade,
sentences.zh: 也就是说，如果我在一个更好的幼儿园教室里，我在幼儿园结束时表现更好，但在一年级结束时只稍微好一点，

sentences.en: and by the time I'm in second or third grade, my performance on standardized tests basically looks comparable to other kids who were in different classes.
sentences.zh: 等我上二年级或三年级时，我在标准化考试中的表现基本上看起来与在不同班级的其他孩子相当。

sentences.en: So, that, I think, that fade-out pattern led to a lot of discouragement among education researchers, saying, oh, it looks like these interventions that we're all studying,
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为，这种消退的模式导致教育研究人员感到非常沮丧，他们说，哦，看起来我们都在研究的这些干预措施，

sentences.en: reducing class size, trying to improve teacher quality, so forth, they seem to have some impacts, but these impacts don't seem to laSt.
sentences.zh: 减小班级规模，试图提高教师质量等等，它们似乎有一些影响，但这些影响似乎并不持久。

sentences.en: So, you know, is this kind of a losing cause in the long run?
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，从长远来看，这算是一种必输的事业吗？

sentences.en: But Raj had a hunch that maybe the long-term research had not tracked the kids long enough.
sentences.zh: 但拉吉有一种直觉，也许长期研究对孩子们的追踪时间还不够长。

sentences.en: He found data from an older experiment from Tennessee.
sentences.zh: 他找到了来自田纳西州一项较早实验的数据。

sentences.en: The students in this experiment had been randomly assigned to different kindergarten classrooms within their schools.
sentences.zh: 这个实验中的学生被随机分配到他们学校内的不同幼儿园教室。

sentences.en: Some had small class sizes of about 15 students.
sentences.zh: 有些班级规模较小，大约15名学生。

sentences.en: Others were placed in classes that had about 25 students.
sentences.zh: 其他学生则被安排在拥有约25名学生的班级里。

sentences.en: Raj and his colleagues did something novel with the data to discover the long-term, the really long-term effects of kindergarten classrooms on students.
sentences.zh: 拉吉和他的同事对这些数据做了一些新颖的处理，以发现幼儿园教室对学生的长期、真正长期的影响。

sentences.en: We take kind of a big data approach and link the school district records for those 12,000 kids to income tax records and social security records many years later that basically allow us to ask,
sentences.zh: 我们采用了一种大数据的方法，将这12,000名孩子的学区记录与多年后的所得税记录和社会保障记录联系起来，这基本上使我们能够询问，

sentences.en: how did your earnings, when you're, say, 25 or 30 years old, vary depending upon which kindergarten classroom you were assigned to?
sentences.zh: 当你比如25岁或30岁时，你的收入如何根据你被分到的幼儿园教室而有所不同？

sentences.en: So what this allows you to do is go beyond asking, what are the impacts of these interventions on test scores,
sentences.zh: 所以这能让你超越去问这些干预措施对考试成绩的影响，

sentences.en: and ask, what are the impacts on things we actually care about at the end of the day?
sentences.zh: 而是去问，对我们最终真正关心的事物有什么影响？

sentences.en: The types of jobs people end up getting, how much they're earning, whether they go to college or not, and so forth.
sentences.zh: 人们最终从事的工作类型、他们的收入、他们是否上大学等等。

sentences.en: And what you end up finding in a nutshell is actually quite striking, which is even though you see this fade-out pattern that I was describing in terms of test score achievement,
sentences.zh: 简而言之，你最终发现的东西实际上非常惊人，也就是说，尽管你在考试成绩方面看到了我一直在描述的这种消退模式，

sentences.en: the gains actually re-emerge in adulthood.
sentences.zh: 但这些收益实际上在成年期重新显现了。

sentences.en: The children who were assigned to better teachers, to smaller classes, are doing significantly better as adults,
sentences.zh: 被分配到更好老师、更小班级的儿童作为成年人表现得明显更好，

sentences.en: showing that early childhood education does, in fact, have lasting impacts,
sentences.zh: 这表明幼儿教育确实具有持久的影响，

sentences.en: even though, curiously, those impacts don't seem to last in terms of test scores.
sentences.zh: 尽管奇怪的是，这些影响在考试成绩方面似乎并不持久。

sentences.en: I mean, it's a remarkable finding, because I think when most of us think about it, we sort of say, well, schooling is important.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一个了不起的发现，因为我想当我们大多数人思考这个问题时，我们都会说，嗯，学校教育很重要。

sentences.en: But if you were to ask me, does what happened in kindergarten affect you when you're 30 years old,
sentences.zh: 但如果你问我，幼儿园发生的事情是否会影响30岁的你，

sentences.en: I would have to say it's probably really marginal.
sentences.zh: 我不得不说这可能微乎其微。

sentences.en: But that's not what you're finding.
And so to be clear, it is one of many, many different things that matters, right?
sentences.zh: 为了明确起见，这是至关重要的许多不同事情之一，对吧？

sentences.en: So I would not say the kindergarten classroom that you're in sort of determines your fate.
sentences.zh: 所以我不会说你所在的幼儿园教室决定了你的命运。

sentences.en: It's one of 100 things that influences your outcomes.
sentences.zh: 它是影响你结果的100个因素之一。

sentences.en: However, if, on average, you're assigned to a better teacher or to a smaller class,
sentences.zh: 然而，如果平均而言，你被分配到一个更好的老师或更小的班级，

sentences.en: we see measurable improvements in children's outcomes on the order of thousands of dollars of earnings per year.
sentences.zh: 我们看到儿童的结果有可测量的改善，金额达到每年数千美元的收入。

sentences.en: And so the kind of quantification of that that we put out in that paper is you can think of having a better kindergarten teacher
sentences.zh: 所以我们在那篇论文中公布的量化结果是，你可以认为拥有一个更好的幼儿园老师

sentences.en: as being worth something like $300,000 for a classroom of students.
sentences.zh: 对一个班级的学生来说价值约30万美元。

sentences.en: That $300,000 figure is an estimate of how much more the kids in the class would earn over their lifetimes.
sentences.zh: 30万美元这个数字是对班里孩子们一生中会多赚多少钱的估计。

sentences.en: It's the difference between the earnings from a class with a high-quality kindergarten teacher
sentences.zh: 这是来自拥有高质量幼儿园老师的班级的收入

sentences.en: and a class with an average teacher.
sentences.zh: 与拥有普通老师的班级的收入之间的差异。

sentences.en: While Raj has found a way to quantify the economic value of a great kindergarten teacher,
sentences.zh: 虽然拉吉找到了一种量化伟大幼儿园老师的经济价值的方法，

sentences.en: he's found it harder to identify what exactly makes a great kindergarten teacher.
sentences.zh: 但他发现很难确定究竟是什么造就了一位伟大的幼儿园老师。

sentences.en: It turns out that credentials, like where a teacher went to college,
sentences.zh: 事实证明，资历，比如老师在哪里上的大学，

sentences.en: are not very helpful in predicting whether someone's going to be a good teacher.
sentences.zh: 对预测某人是否会成为好老师并没有太大帮助。

sentences.en: So Raj looked instead at how teachers taught their students.
sentences.zh: 因此，拉吉转而研究老师是如何教学生的。

sentences.en: It's less about, you know, you're very good at explaining certain mathematical concepts
sentences.zh: 这与其说是因为，你知道的，你非常擅长解释某些数学概念，

sentences.en: and something a little bit more nebulous about how well, for instance,
sentences.zh: 不如说是一些更捉摸不透的东西，比如，举个例子，

sentences.en: you're able to manage a classroom of small children, some of whom might end up being disruptive.
sentences.zh: 你管理一小群幼儿的能力有多强，其中一些人最后可能会具有破坏性。

sentences.en: Are you able to keep people focused?
sentences.zh: 你能让大家保持专注吗？

sentences.en: Are you able to inspire people?
How you go about measuring those things systematically, I think, is a very interesting question.
sentences.zh: 我认为，你将如何系统地去衡量这些事情，是一个非常有趣的问题。

sentences.en: And even more importantly, how can we then perhaps train teachers to do better on those dimensions?
sentences.zh: 更重要的是，我们接下来该如何培训老师，让他们在这些维度上做得更好？
那将具有极其宝贵的价值。

sentences.en: But at the moment, I think the best summary is we don't quite know yet.
